diagnosis: The issue lies in the DFA state transitions, particularly at line 463. The current implementation does not correctly handle the transition when encountering a semicolon ';' which should trigger comment processing but instead leads to incorrect tokenization.

causal_chain: Line 463 computes next_state based on base[state] - ch >=0, which may fail for certain characters like ';'
This failure causes the DFA to not transition into a comment-skipping state
As a result, subsequent characters are treated as separate tokens instead of being ignored as part of a comment

uncertainty: While multiple approaches could potentially fix the issue, the most straightforward repair is to modify line 463 to handle ';' as a special case triggering comment skipping. This approach maintains minimal changes while directly addressing the observed failures in MR2-MR5 test cases.
assumption: Adjust the base and next arrays to correctly route ';' to a skip state

edits.rationale: Ensure that ';' transitions lead to comment skipping
edits.replacement: if (base[state] - ch >=0 && (state != INITIAL || ch != ';')) { ... } else if(ch == ';') { return(SKIP_COMMENT); }

expected_effect: Correctly transition to comment skip on ';' without affecting other transitions
preservation_constraints: Other token transitions must remain functional
